Capex 2010 US$: stated in the Table 5 header 'Typical current international values for new installed capacity (2010 US$)'; the p.6 text gives the same range with no year. Table 4 renewable-desalination costs (sidecar) are converted from EUR at 1.3 USD/EUR with no currency year.

Main file (a thin proxy for industrial water treatment - the brief is municipal seawater/brackish desalination): conventional RO, ED, MSF and MED from Tables 3 and 5 as one process 'Conventional water desalination (Tables 3 and 5)' - energy per m3 - RO and ED electricity as specific-energy-consumption and flows; MSF and MED as DERIVED total (printed thermal + electricity) specific-energy-consumption plus separate electricity and heat (steam) flows - the merged capex 800-1500 2010 USD per m3/day and the merged average plant size 4000-5000 m3/day recorded on each column; and the Perth SWRO plant (3.4 kWh/m3). Vapour compression has no conventional energy figure (na). Sidecars: _renewable-desalination (Table 4: solar, PV and wind couplings - renewable power supply, levelized water costs, mostly R&D) and _context (process temperatures, market shares, O&M %, water production costs, global figures). Candidate archetypes: RO and ED -> separator_reverse-osmosis (seawater proxy); MSF and MED -> no close archetype (nearest: separator_reverse-osmosis 'evaporative concentration' or evaporator_crystallizer, which is MVC).

(1) Table 5 renewable block heads its energy row 'kWhe/m3 + kJt/kg', but the thermal values (100, <200, 60-70) are kWh/m3 as in Table 4. (2) O&M: Table 5 1.5-2.5% of investment per year vs p.6 text 'about 2-2.5%'. (3) PV/RO seawater cost: Table 4 12-15.6 vs Table 5 11.7-15.6 USD/m3. (4) Table 5 omits Table 4's Wind/RO 1000 m3/d cost (2-5.2). (5) Solar stills capacity '<0.1' (Table 4) printed '0,1' in Table 5. (6) p.6 average energy demands (MSF 5, RO 2.5 kWh/m3) contradict Table 3 (MSF 2.5-3.5, RO 3.5-5.0). (7) Table 3 footnote defines SWRO as 'Spiral wound reverse osmosis'. (8) MED thermal energy printed identical to MSF (80.6 kWh/m3, 290 kJ/kg) in both tables - possible copied cell. (9) p.2 highlights: 80 kWh 'about 290 MJ' - 80 kWh is 288 MJ per m3, i.e. 290 kJ/kg; the MJ is per m3, not stated. (10) Typos: 'costal', 'Adbulaziz', 'Abs El Aleem' vs 'Abd El Aleem' in the references.
